choices.content: The probability that \(A\) and \(B\) both occur, divided by \(P(B)\)

question.prompt: What is the definition of \(P(A\mid B)\)?

solutions.explanation:
Conditional probability restricts the sample space to the part where \(B\) has occurred. When \(P(B)>0\), we divide the probability that both events occur by \(P(B)\):
\[
P(A\mid B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}.
\]
The ratio is undefined when \(P(B)=0\). Therefore the correct definition is choice D.
solutions.title: State the defining ratio
